correctness.rationale: The definition of the weak covering index is proved equivalent to \(\inf_{0<\lambda<1}N_\lambda(K)/(1-\lambda)\), with both directions handling possible non-attainment of \(\gamma_m\). Bezdek--Khan Proposition 4.2 applies because all parallelotope coordinate segments are tightly covered, yielding \(N_\lambda(K\oplus C^r)=N_\lambda(K)\lceil1/\lambda\rceil^r\). The ceiling is at least \(2\), giving the lower bound, and is exactly \(2\) at any attaining ratio in \([1/2,1)\). Their exact triangle and hexagon data at \(\lambda=2/3\) then give the stated infinite families.

originality.rationale: Bezdek--Khan explicitly state that no suitable weak analogue of their ordinary one-codimensional cylinder corollary is available and therefore list only upper estimates \(\le18\) for the hexagonal and triangular cylinders. The new variational observation supplies a conditional weak cylinder law and proves those estimates exact, then extends them to arbitrary cube codimension. A 2020 full-text paper on covering functionals of direct sums was checked and does not state the weak-index result. Candidate-specific searches found no implication-equivalent statement.

value.rationale: The introducing paper explicitly identifies the lack of a useful weak cylinder analogue as the reason it can only estimate one-codimensional cylinders. The result supplies a structural conditional analogue, closes both concrete estimates printed in that table, and produces the exact infinite families \(9\cdot2^r\). It therefore resolves an exposed quantitative gap rather than recomputing a known invariant.
